Trigger is "user uses an action" and result is "cast scrying with fixed DC". The printed base Crystal Ball clause requires touching the ball (SRD pp. 214-215) and supplies no action-speed casting exception. SRD p. 207 / rule:spells retains the spell's normal casting time; Scrying takes 10 minutes (pp. 176-177 / spell:scrying). An attuned user who is not touching the ball spending an action is therefore admitted by the emitted trigger although the source forbids that use; the same trigger also represents casting as a single-action event instead of retaining normal casting time. No enclosing parent operation, state machine or eligibility projection supplies the touch prerequisite or correct timing. The nearby variant text's one-action detect thoughts/suggestion permissions do not authorize changing the parent Scrying clause.
2. magic-item:dimensional-shackles / c2-residual-dimensional-movement-block: magicItemResidualCombatEffects.ts:867-868; records.json:97902. The effect asserts immunity to extradimensional movement, with travel to another plane as an example, but omits the source's explicit interdimensional-portal exception (SRD p. 219). A bound creature walking through a Gate portal to another plane is permitted by the source yet falls within the effect's unqualified travel-to-another-plane prohibition. The enclosing bound-state/operations contain no portal exception. This changes the scope of the prohibition already projected; it is not an independent omitted item power.
3. magic-item:dust-of-dryness / c2-residual-water-elemental-damage: magicItemResidualCombatEffects.ts:894; records.json:98639. Source p. 219 triggers when a mostly-water elemental is EXPOSED to a pinch. The residual effect instead requires the pinch to be THROWN AT it. Sprinkling a pinch directly onto the elemental exposes it without throwing and triggers the printed DC 13 / 10d6 necrotic procedure, but not this projection. Inspected sprinkle-dust activation and the separately emitted absorb-water payload: they use sprinkling/exposure, so the enclosing record does not establish throwing as a prerequisite and instead contains disagreeing accounts of the same damage clause. A correct duplicate does not make each emitted effect source-agreeing.
